postText:
SEO & AI Tip: A Semantic Map shows exactly where competitors have more coverage than you on a topic or keyword. It can also highlight how much more aligned they are with topical intent.

You can measure where competitors beat you on a topic, and where the open gaps are, by plotting your pages, their pages, and your target keywords in the same vector space.

You no longer need to size up the competition by eyeballing their content and counting how many articles they've published.

This is one piece of a larger Semantic Audit, but it's the piece that turns "they seem to cover this better" into a measurable, side-by-side picture.

comments.text: If a model allowed you to parse the full page's content in one go, would you say chunking is still required?
What are the embedding models that you use?
Semantic mapping turns vague SEO assumptions into something measurable and actually actionable.

postText:
Most SEO tools score pages.
AI search engines retrieve passages.

That difference matters.

I built a free "Semantic Relevance Analyzer" to help SEOs, content teams, and business owners understand which parts of their content are semantically aligned with a target query, and which sections are weakening the page.

Instead of checking keyword density, the tool breaks content into passages and scores each section against your target keyword or prompt using vector similarity.

comments.text: Passage-level scoring is a much better way to look at relevance for AI search.
Scoring individual passages instead of the whole page is a much better way to look at relevance.
